notes: Restoration druid healer rotation (stage 2 of the healer build), written against the fork's fake raid: the healer is raid player 0, the four fake party members are players 1 to 4 and the tank is player 5. The tank carries Regrowth and Rejuvenation for the whole fight (Nature's Splendor makes them 27 and 15 seconds), Healing Touch fires only on a real hole in his health bar and only while the mana bar is above the share of the fight left, so the mana lasts instead of running out at the first long fight. Party members get Rejuvenation when one is hurt and Tranquility when two are well down. Nature's Swiftness is cast by hand and always with an instant Healing Touch under 35% tank health, the major-cooldown pass is told to leave it alone for a healer. Rejuvenation is cast below the top rank on purpose: on the party rank 7 in a raid and rank 1 below 60 and without raid buffs (rank 2 at 26 to 29 and at 40 to 42, rank 4 at 44 and rank 5 at 45 to 48; the round 18 to 30 rows), and on the tank rank 10 in a raid; below 60 the tank's rank follows the level (rank 1 to 22, rank 2 at 23 to 39 with rank 3 at 29 for a night elf, rank 4 at 40 to 43, rank 5 at 44 to 48, rank 6 at 49 to 55, rank 9 at 56 to 58, rank 8 at 59; the rank-choice rows, re-judged level by level in rounds 19 to 30); their lines say why. The Healing Touch filler (not the Nature's Swiftness save) also drops below the top rank while leveling: rank 2 at 20 and, for a tauren, 21 to 23, rank 3 at 30 to 33, rank 4 at 34 to 39, rank 5 at 40 to 45 and rank 6 at 46 to 48 (round 18 to 24 rank-choice rows, lines [9]). Every other heal casts the top rank. Healing Touch rank 11 and Rejuvenation rank 11 are Ahn'Qiraj book ranks (core.IncludeAQ is false), so the top ranks are 10; the client's second Regrowth and Rejuvenation ids (436937-436946, 417057-417068) are not taught by the trainer and are not used. Client 1.60.1.70707 (2026-10-31): the Wild Growth line is gone. The guide build does not take the talent (heal-builds measured it about 5% less healing for any point it would take, with Wild Growth's new 3 s cast), so the line could never fire for it and a player reading the rotation cannot cast it. Round 6 (design/reviews/2026-11-02-sim-audit-round6/healers.md): the heal profile's raid-wide pulses now land on the healer as well, three of the five members of the group a pulse. You are a party member like the other four: Rejuvenation covers you and Tranquility counts you (about +0.8% effective healing against the same list without you). Wild Growth was measured again on this fight, with the point from Swiftmend and 36 Wild Growth lines: the best was level with this list, within error, so the build and the list stand. Measured once more on 2026-11-12 (sim-healers lane), after the 10 Nov hotfix made Nature's Swiftness cover it and client 70888 doubled its tick coefficient: the guide's Wild Growth build with a party line ahead of Tranquility, after the tank lines on the mana pace, or on any hurt member, loses 1.7 to 18.9% at band 60, so the build and the list still stand.

Forever Sixty default rotation, unvalidated until the nightly job runs

priorityList.notes: On yourself below 30% mana. It multiplies your Spirit regeneration, and a Restoration druid carries a lot of Spirit.

Alliance Skyborne only: Read Leyline every time it is ready. 50% more mana regeneration for 15 seconds is worth a global cooldown on a fight that drains your mana bar. It will not cast under Innervate, and an Innervate replaces it.
When the tank drops under 35%: Nature's Swiftness, then an instant Healing Touch on him.
Right after Nature's Swiftness, as the instant save on the tank.
When the tank is under 75% and your mana is keeping pace with the fight. In Forever it does not use up the HoT, so it is a heal of its own on a 15 second cooldown, for 20% of your base mana.
When two of your party, you included, are under 70% at once. It heals the whole party every 2 seconds.
On the tank once he is below 90% and it is not ticking. Let it run out before you recast it: from 20, Bloom heals him when it does. At 18 and 19 rank 1 heals more for your mana than rank 2.

On the tank once he is below 97% and it is not ticking, at rank 10 in a raid. Let it run out before you recast it: from 20, Bloom heals him when it does. While leveling your mana runs out first, so a lower rank heals more for it: rank 1 at 10 (a Skyborne keeps rank 2) and from 13 to 22 (from 12 for an Alliance Skyborne), rank 2 from 23 to 39 (a night elf takes rank 3 for level 29 alone), rank 4 from 40 to 43, rank 5 from 44 to 48, rank 6 from 49 to 55, rank 9 from 56 to 58 and rank 8 at 59.

On the tank under 55%, only while your mana is ahead of the fight. While leveling, a lower rank heals more for the mana than the top rank: rank 2 from 14 to 16 (a night elf and either Skyborne drop to rank 1 at 15 and 16, and a Horde Skyborne casts rank 1 from 13), rank 1 from 17 to 19, rank 2 at 20 (a tauren keeps it to 23, and takes rank 4 at 26 to 28), rank 3 from 30 to 33, rank 4 from 34 to 39, rank 5 from 40 to 45 and rank 6 from 46 to 48.

On a hurt party member under 70%, you included. It does not wait on the mana pace the costly heals follow. While leveling, rank 1 heals the most for your mana, except rank 2 at 10 to 14 (a night elf takes rank 1 at 10, a Horde Skyborne rank 1 from 13, and a tauren rank 3 at 16), 26 to 29 (25 too for an Alliance druid) and 40 to 42, rank 4 at 44 and rank 5 at 45 to 48.

Rejuvenation on anyone in your party below 90%, you included, while your mana % is over boss health %: in a raid the group's small hits add up, and a ticking Rejuvenation clears them before the next one lands. Rank 7 in a raid.
